title: Open Appendectomy
references: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery: the vermiform appendix, appendicectomy
Farquharson's Textbook of Operative General Surgery: open appendicectomy
Gray's Anatomy: the caecum and vermiform appendix, the anterior abdominal wall
todo: The whole sequence needs checking by a qualified surgeon before it is marked reviewed.
Bleeding rates (bleedMlPerSecond) are schematic figures chosen to make the vitals monitor move, not measured losses.
Ties are modelled with the needle holder and the suture action until the engine has a ligate action (open question from Phase 2).
Prep and draping are not steps: the patient starts draped. Whether to add them is open.

steps.title: Make the skin incision
steps.objective: Incise the skin over McBurney's point.
steps.explanation: McBurney's point overlies the usual position of the base of the appendix, so an incision here gives the most direct access.
hints: Find the line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.
McBurney's point is a third of the way along it from the spine.

commonErrors.feedback: Too far from McBurney's point. Find the line from the spine to the umbilicus first.

quiz.question: Where is McBurney's point?
options: One third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus
Midway between the umbilicus and the pubic symphysis
Two thirds of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus
quiz.answer: One third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus

steps.todo: Confirm which skin incision to teach (oblique gridiron or transverse Lanz) and its length; the scene draws the line from this.

steps.title: Deepen through the fat
steps.objective: Divide the subcutaneous fat down to the external oblique aponeurosis.
steps.explanation: Diathermy through the fat seals the small vessels as it goes, so the wound stays dry enough to see the layer beneath.
hints: Stay in the line of the skin incision.
Stop when you reach the shiny aponeurosis.

steps.title: Open the external oblique
steps.objective: Open the external oblique aponeurosis in the line of its fibres.
steps.explanation: Cutting along the fibres rather than across them splits the layer without dividing it, so it heals strongly when closed.
hints: Follow the direction the fibres run.

commonErrors.feedback: That is not the external oblique. Clear the fat until you see its fibres.

quiz.question: Which way do the fibres of the external oblique run?

steps.title: Split the muscles
steps.objective: Split internal oblique and transversus along their fibres and hold them apart.
steps.explanation: Splitting the muscles rather than cutting them keeps their nerve supply and strength, which is why this approach is called muscle-splitting.
hints: These fibres run in a different direction from the external oblique.
steps.todo: Confirm the teaching description of the blunt split (closed scissors or clamp, then retractors) before content describes the technique in more detail.

steps.title: Open the peritoneum
steps.objective: Lift the peritoneum and open it.
steps.explanation: Bowel lies directly beneath the peritoneum. Lifting it away first means the cut goes through the peritoneum alone.
hints: Tent it up away from what lies beneath before you cut.

commonErrors.feedback: That is small bowel. Lift the peritoneum clear before you cut.

steps.title: Deliver the caecum
steps.objective: Grasp the caecum gently and bring it into the wound.
steps.explanation: Working with the caecum in the wound keeps the rest of the abdomen out of the field.
hints: Babcock forceps hold bowel without crushing it.

commonErrors.feedback: That is small bowel, not caecum. Look for the taeniae coli.
Bowel is handled with atraumatic forceps.

steps.title: Find and deliver the appendix
steps.objective: Follow the taeniae coli to the base of the appendix and bring the appendix up.
steps.explanation: The taeniae coli meet at the base of the appendix, so they lead to it wherever its tip lies.
hints: Trace a taenia along the caecum.
Where the taeniae meet, the appendix begins.

quiz.question: What leads you to the base of the appendix?
options: The meeting point of the taeniae coli
quiz.answer: The meeting point of the taeniae coli

steps.title: Clamp the mesoappendix
steps.objective: Clamp the mesoappendix, which carries the appendicular artery.
steps.explanation: The appendicular artery runs in the mesoappendix, so it is controlled before the mesoappendix is divided.
hints: The mesoappendix is the fold that joins the appendix to the ileum's mesentery.

quiz.question: The appendicular artery is usually a branch of which artery?

steps.todo: Confirm whether to teach the mesoappendix taken in one clamp or in serial bites.

steps.title: Divide the mesoappendix
steps.objective: Divide the mesoappendix on the appendix side of the clamp.
steps.explanation: Cutting on the side that is coming out leaves the clamp holding the vessel that stays.
hints: Keep the clamp on the side of the tissue that stays in the patient.

steps.title: Tie the mesoappendix
steps.explanation: A clamp is temporary. The tie is what keeps the artery closed once the clamp comes off.
hints: Tie beneath the clamp, then release the clamp.
steps.todo: Ligature material and size are not given; confirm what to teach.

steps.title: Crush the base
steps.objective: Crush the base of the appendix with a clamp.
steps.explanation: Crushing leaves a groove where the tie will sit securely.
hints: Right at the base, where it joins the caecum.

commonErrors.feedback: Too far along the appendix. The clamp goes at its base.

steps.title: Tie the base
steps.objective: Tie the base of the appendix in the crushed groove.
steps.explanation: The tie closes the stump so that the caecum stays sealed once the appendix is removed.
hints: Move the clamp a little further along first, and tie in the groove it left.
steps.todo: Ligature material and size are not given; confirm what to teach.

steps.title: Remove the appendix
steps.objective: Divide the appendix between the tie and the clamp.
steps.explanation: The tie holds the stump closed and the clamp holds the appendix end, so nothing spills when it is cut.
hints: Cut between the tie and the clamp.
steps.todo: How the stump is dealt with after this (left, or buried with a purse-string) varies; confirm what to teach.

steps.title: Check for bleeding
steps.objective: Check the stump and the mesoappendix for bleeding.
steps.explanation: Bleeding is easiest to deal with now, while the tied stump and pedicle are still in view.

steps.title: Return the caecum
steps.objective: Return the caecum to the abdomen.
steps.explanation: The caecum goes back before the layers are closed over it.

steps.title: Close the peritoneum
steps.explanation: Closing the deep layer first rebuilds the abdominal wall from the inside out.

commonErrors.feedback: That bite would catch bowel. Keep the needle in the peritoneum.

steps.todo: Whether the peritoneum is closed as a separate layer varies; confirm, and the suture to use.

steps.title: Bring the muscles together
steps.objective: Loosely bring internal oblique and transversus back together.
steps.explanation: The split muscles only need to lie together again; they were never cut.
steps.todo: Confirm whether this layer is sutured and with what.

steps.title: Close the external oblique
steps.explanation: The aponeurosis is the strength layer of this closure.
steps.todo: Suture material, size and technique are not given; confirm what to teach.

steps.title: Close the skin
steps.explanation: The skin closure is the part the patient sees; even spacing and edges that meet give the neatest scar.
hints: The suturing pad drill practises this.
steps.todo: Confirm the skin closure to teach (interrupted, subcuticular or staples) and the suture.
